_schema.description: Seat-level models, one entry per district per model: MRP polls (by hand; an MRP replaced by a newer one from the same pollster stays as history with superseded_by and is no longer counted; one only partly replaced (the newer one published for some seats) has updated_by and still counts, the newer one taking its place in the seats it covers), Australian Election Forecasts (aeforecasts.com, refreshed by scripts/refresh.py every run) and RedBridge's seat model (statewide totals, by hand; refresh.py warns when RedBridge's site shows a newer Victorian release). null = not published.

fields.models: [{id, source, kind (mrp | forecast | projection), name, credit, client, fieldwork, sample_size, published, model_date (forecast: when the model was run) or published_date (YYYY-MM-DD), label, source_url, data_url, notes; superseded_by and superseded_on (an older model kept as history: pages count only published models without superseded_by); updated_by (a newer model from the same pollster published for only some seats: this one still counts, including in the seat totals, but in each seat the newer one gives a winner or runner-up for, the newer one is used instead); via [{label, url, districts}] (where hand-entered seat figures were read, when the pollster's own release couldn't be); seats_published (how many districts have figures, when not all 88); forecasts also fp_percentiles and expected_seats {bloc: sum of win probabilities}; projections also inputs {poll, primary} and totals {bloc: seats, toss_up}, toss_ups ([district ids] or null if not published)}]
fields.district: id of the district in districts.json
fields.model: id of the model in models
fields.winner: Predicted winner party code (ALP, LIB, NAT, LNP, GRN, ONP, IND, OTH) or null if not published
fields.winner_name: Forecasts: the winning candidate's name as the model gives it
fields.runner_up: Predicted runner-up party code or null
fields.win_probability: Predicted probability (0-100) the winner takes the seat, or null if not published
fields.candidates: Forecasts: [{name, party, win_probability (0-100), fp [low, central, high] first-preference %}], fp at the model's fp_percentiles
fields.others: Forecasts: [{label, party, win_probability, fp}] for outcomes without a named candidate (others, an emerging independent or party)
fields.two_cp: Forecasts: [{parties [A, B], probability (0-100) of that final pairing, share [low, central, high] of A's 2CP %}]
fields.note: Optional: what a hand-entered row's figures cover where they are incomplete (e.g. a winner not stated)

models.name: YouGov MRP (Jul 2026)
models.notes: Projected winner, runner-up and winner's 2CP share from the report's per-seat table. No win probabilities published. Fieldwork predates the July 2026 Labor leadership change. Still counted (decided 26 Nov 2026), including in the home page's seat projection, because YouGov's November MRP is held for six seats only; in those six seats the November figures are used instead.

models.name: YouGov MRP (Nov 2026)

via.label: The Conversation (Adrian Beaumont, 25 Nov 2026), as republished by Yahoo News: 2CP

models.notes: The Herald Sun and News24 publish YouGov's projection for every seat, but both are News Corp sites whose robots.txt disallows all agents, so only the seats reported by The Conversation, Yahoo News and The Poll Bludger are stored; the other 82 are null (not read). No statewide seat totals were found in a source we may read, so this model doesn't count in the home page's seat projection (an MRP counts only with a winner in all 88); the July MRP still does, and in these six seats this model replaces it. Niddrie: Labor projected to lose 43-57, the winning party not stated. Win likelihoods published for Bendigo East and Mulgrave only.

models.name: DemosAU MRP
models.notes: No Victorian seat-level DemosAU MRP found as of 30 Oct 2026 (DemosAU's October MRP was federal; its September Victorian release was a seat projection from a statewide poll, not per-seat). Entries left blank.

models.name: RedBridge seat model
models.notes: RedBridge's seat model run on the latest Newspoll's statewide primaries, posted on LinkedIn by RedBridge's Kosmos Samaras (date read from the post's id). Statewide totals only: no per-seat ratings, and the six toss-up seats aren't recorded here (LinkedIn can't be read by scripts). Add them to toss_ups by hand if needed.

models.name: Australian Election Forecasts
models.label: Final pre-election forecast
models.notes: Win probabilities and first-preference ranges per candidate, from the model's simulations. fp and share are [5th percentile, median, 95th percentile]; two_cp lists the final pairings with at least 1% chance, share being the first party's 2CP %. 'An emerging independent/party' is the model's allowance for a strong candidate not yet named.

seats.note: Labor (Ben Carroll) projected to lose 43-57; the winning party isn't stated in the sources read.
Runner-up as The Poll Bludger reads the projection (Greens second, on 14% of first preferences); the 54-46 opponent isn't named.
